doc.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Mongo Santamaria and early recording sessions
title: Wes Montgomery, Don Sebesky and Jimmy Smith dates
summary: Laws did not know he was on Wes Montgomery's Down Here on the Ground, probably via Creed Taylor. Brown lists Sebesky's and Jimmy Smith's dates.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: How about the one with Wes Montgomery, Down Here on the Ground?
I played on that? I just heard that on the radio today. I didn’t know I played on it, though. Creed probably got me involved in that. What year was that?
It must have been at Rudy’s place, too.
I didn’t know I played on that. I know that record. I’ve heard it. But I didn’t know I played on it.

When I told Ken about it, I said, “I remember my dad had this,” because I remember the cover. Because my dad – oh yeah. Like I say, you’re the soundtrack to my entire . . . Then, Don Sebesky and the Jazz-Rock Syndrome, Don Sebesky big band. I hadn’t actually heard this. It’s got – kind of interesting. Then Jimmy Smith, Stay Loose. It’s a pretty big band.
